replies.title: (no subject)
replies.content:
That's something about which occult writers disagree sharply. Some people insist that those are two names for the same thing. I think they're wrong, partly because of my experiences and partly because I tend to rely on Dion Fortune, who also had a little bit of experience in these matters.

As I see it, there are two things involved here, aside from the lower self or personality -- that's the ordinary self you call "me." The first of them is the higher self or individuality. This isn't a separate being from you -- it's who you really are. Your personality is a mask (the word "personality" comes from a Latin word for "mask"). What's under the mask is the individuality or higher self, the self that survives death and passes through the cycles of reincarnation -- what Zen masters call the face you had before your mother and father were born.

The guardian angel or guardian genius is something else again. It's a wholly separate entity from you, an emanation from the Divine, and its task is to help you in your spiritual development. It can't make you do anything. All it can do is advise you, and you have to pay attention to it; it can express itself as intuition, insight, the voice of conscience, or what have you. Workings to come into closer contact with this entity are very useful because it has a much broader perspective than you do, and the better you can hear it, the easier a time you'll have in your spiritual work and in your life as a whole.

replies.content:
A more specific part of that "we don't know" has to do with what economists call "returns to scale" or "decreasing marginal costs". If you have, as one of the things that's ubiquitously available in the background, a huge built-up basic structure of shared propensities and field-tested wisdom that guardian geniuses would need in order to help, then it very well might not take that much in the way of extra resources to take a bit of that energy and special-case it so that it's acting responsively to the particular circumstances of some single soul. That being the case, given that the genius on average increases the efficiency of the process of the soul's development, the optimal resource allocation might have the amount allocated to there being a specialized guardian genius (of the optimal level of activity) go in some linear or slightly sublinear proportion to the amount allocated to there being a soul (having that soul's particular level of complexity/development/weight) in the first place. So, within that hypothesis, it shouldn't be surprising to see guardian geniuses under just the same circumstances as you should expect to see souls in the first place. To some extent there's also a perspective shift on this same idea, where you re-describe it as, well a lot of what's going on with the effects and dynamics of that soul is actually driven by the details of the group soul it participates in, and the more-expensive guardian genius is allocated to that group soul.

To whatever extent each soul is extremely sui generis from the get-go, then the logic within the above speculation doesn't work; the investment needed to build up that huge basic structure doesn't pay off. But empirically there's a lot in common between souls (insofar as we can even tell).

(If one syncretizes western occultism with transhumanist speculation, the first things one might think of as being limited "resources" are computation and memory. But, that aside, "resources" can also include connectivity, like, positions in webs where the elements of the web are making competing claims on each others' attention or influence. Or, for that matter, claims on each others' conflict-resolution effort -- there's a theory that, in the animal kingdom, "consciousness" in the commonplace sense first arises as a conflict-resolution mechanism, capable of learning from the outcomes from resolving any given conflict between some more-"automatic" subsystems to get better at choosing highly-rewarded outcomes from resolving conflicts between those or other more-"automatic" subsystems.)

replies.content:
The difficulty here is that "autism" is a label for a wide range of different conditions which don't have the same effects or concerns. Two autistic people can differ drastically in how they relate to spiritual practices, since autism these days basically embraces anything that isn't normal neurology.

In the hope that it helps, though, here's some of what I've figured out about my own condition.

1) It's a feature of this incarnation only. In my own case, I happen to know what brought it about. I died last time around by having my head go through a windshield in a messy head-on collision. Had certain life choices gone differently, I would have survived, but I'd have had a traumatic brain injury to deal with -- and my symptoms in this life are not wholly unlike that kind of TBI. There's old karma tied up in the experience, which I had to deal with one way or another. As I've gotten older, interestingly, the intensity of my symptoms has gradually decreased, just as though my brain was healing.

2) It's very idiosyncratic. I need silence for spiritual practice, for example; I discovered this spring, along these lines, that the reason that standard Christian church services have always seemed spiritually empty to me is that all the music and singing make it impossible for me to perceive anything spiritual. (It's as though fifty people were all trying to talk to me at once, loudly.) Other people, including other autistic people, don't have this problem. replies.content:
"As I've gotten older, interestingly, the intensity of my symptoms has gradually decreased, just as though my brain was healing."

According to some hypotheses, this lessening of symptoms isn't because your brain is healing but because it's dying. Autistics are known to have higher density of brain cells as well as more synapses, there are theories that the main causal factor is a lack of apoptosis in the brain that happens during normal development. This could be the cause of symptoms like sensory overloads and obsessive interests.

Human social behavior is dependent on a set of pathways in the brain called the mirror neuron system, and it's likely that this system depends on precise timing to work correctly, and having too much signal traffic prevents it from working. (Taking lots of hallucinogens can also cause temporary autistic-like symptoms, and those drugs also cause signal floods.) But as you get older your brain cells die and this may bring your functioning closer to the baseline, having similar brain density to a neurotypical, with the benefit that in your twilight years you may simply be "normal" rather than senile.

That depends on where you draw the line between yourself and not-yourself, and that's a far more complex matter than most people realize. Some of what transforms the universe as it is into the things we experience is hardwired into physics -- the behavior of light waves, for example. comments.title: Formulaire de la Haute magie - Piobb
comments.content:
Hi JMG,

Are you familiar with the work of Pierre Piobb? I found a copy of the second edition (1937) of his Formulaire de la Haute Magie, first published in 1907, in a second hand bookstore (where I picked up a bunch of second hand books by Papus at the same time). It is a wide sweep that shows Taoist trigrams, grimoire pantacles, natural magic spells and lots of tables of correspondences for trees, plants, stones. Piobb echoes your sentiment up to a point about the universality of cabala beyond its christian expression through the Jewish alphabet. There is some astrological magic from Picatrix; he mentions Lunar Mansions briefly, and what looks like an attempt to describe renaissance cosmology in the light of contemporary scientific thought.

…parmi les forces d'efficacité générale se range en premier lieu comme la plus constante et la moins variable, celle que les astronomes modernes appellent l'attraction universelle. En vertu de la conception de Newton et selon la loi qui porte son nom, l'attraction est la forme de l'énergie proprement dite qui anime le mouvement des corps céleste dans l'Univers entier; néanmoins Einstein a démontré que, si cette conception devait toujours se considérer comme juste, la loi qui l'exprime n'était applicable - telle qu'elle se trouve énoncée - qu'au "système solaire", étant constaté qu'au delà et pour d'autres "systèmes stellaires" des corrections s'imposaient. Cette observation importante conduit à dire que la forme de l'énergie dénommée attraction est une force agissante dont la transformation en travail présente un aspect particulier dans le "système solaire"; et puisque cet aspect existe, il ne peut provenir que de la constitution même dudit "système solaire".

This is not a great example of understanding physics, but then he says something which I found intriguing about astrological magic:

Donc les forces du monde de la formation sont une spécialisation pour le "système solaire", et conséquemment pour notre planète, des énergies de même catégories qui existent en d'autres "systèmes stellaires". Comme il n'est pas question d'utiliser l'énergie de "réseaux" autres que celui dont la Terre dépend directement (c'est à dire hiérarchiquement), la Magie ne se sert que des forces du monde de la formation dont le siège se trouve dans le "système solaire" et ne considère que les "plasmas sidéraux" qui les représentent et les manifestent.

On another note, I thought it was interesting when looking at his other works to see the table of contents of his book Étude du macrocosme, after reading your book The Twilight of Pluto, to see the list of planets include Ceres but not Pluto, as an illustration of what you were talking about in that book.

I thought I'd bring this up here in case it holds scholarly interest, especially since the book is not yet translated to English, and it seems to have some historical value in the history of magic in the 20th century, very unlike what was published back then but possibly decades, almost a century, ahead of the revival on interest for classical, medieval and renaissance magic.

Best,
JML
